name: Bima
catalog_quote: De klemtoon valt regelmatig op de voorlaatste lettergreep, zeer zelden op de laatste. ... Woorden, die in de taal waaruit zij overgenomen zijn, tweelettergrepig zijn, maar in het Bim. drielettergrepig moeten worden, behouden gewoonlijk hun accent, zoo hebben bijv. putir ... mantari ... kòròma ... sapatu ... den klemtoon op de eerste lettergreep.

audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding quotations (Jonker 1896:11 §3 penult rule with loanword exceptions; §210 p.257 enclitic stress shift) are verbatim in the held archive.org djvu text at the stated places. (2) Deciding source is the standard (and only) reference grammar of Bima, 1896, 487 pp.; the held Owens 2000 MA thesis gives the same penult rule and the same rightward shift under agreement enclitics from fresh fieldwork, so the fixed-penult (WORD domain incl. enclitics) coding is doubly supported and nothing found contradicts it. Jonker's exceptions (initial stress in some trisyllabic loans, final stress in vocatives/with emphatic enclitics and in prefixed monosyllabic roots) are lexical/intonational and already recorded in the source note; they do not change 'fixed-strict penult'. (3) One better-dated source exists and is not held: Tama et al. 1996 Fonologi Bahasa Bima (Pusat Bahasa, 10

Bimaneesche Spraakkunst (Verhandelingen van het Bataviaasch Genootschap XLVIII), p. 11 (§3) and p. 257 (§210) — read via archive.org item verhandelinge48189396bata (djvu full text). Also read: Verheijen 1982, Komodo: het Eiland, het Volk en de Taal, pp. 25 and 41-42 — full text…
sources.quote: "The stress falls regularly on the penultimate syllable, very rarely on the last." (Jonker 1896:11). §210: "They form one whole with the noun to which they are attached and thus make the stress jump to the originally last syllable." — "ana-k (naturally with the stress on the last syllable)".
